newsitem.title: EGYPT: Israel, PLO meet for first time in over two months.
newsitem.headline: Israel, PLO meet for first time in over two months.

text.p: Israeli and Palestinian negotiators met on Sunday for the first time in more than two months after untangling a last-minute snag over Jewish settlements.
They did not speak to reporters as they entered Ittihadia presidential palace in Cairo.
Israeli Ambassador to Egypt Zvi Mazael told reporters earlier: "The Israeli delegation has arrived to see what can be done. People have to talk first. We are hopeful."

The meeting in Cairo had been cast into doubt when Palestinian President Yasser Arafat's spokesman Marwan Kanafani told Reuters that Israel had in principle accepted a "pause" in settlement building activities.
Israel promptly denied this and threatened to refuse to take part in the planned peace talks until the PLO retracted the statement.
In Cairo, senior Palestinian negotiator Saeb Erekat then cleared the way for the meeting by saying Israel had not agreed to preconditions on settlement building.
"There is no agreement with the Israeli side," Erekat told reporters. He said he was not optimistic about the meeting because the two sides still had many disagreements.
The negotiations have been in crisis since Israel broke ground three months ago on the 6,500-unit Jewish settlement of Har Homa on an Arab East Jerusalem hill Palestinians call Jabal Abu Ghneim.

Construction continued at the site on Sunday and witnesses said bulldozers had cut several roads into the hill and concrete and stone retaining walls had been built to buttress the terraces on which houses will be built.
Osama al-Baz, the adviser to Egypt's President Hosni Mubarak who shuttled between the sides this month trying to revive peacemaking, was also attending the Cairo talks.

Israeli officials insisted that Netanyahu's right-wing government remained committed to building Jewish settlements on occupied land in the West Bank, including in Arab East Jerusalem, as well as in the Gaza Strip.
More than 130,000 Jews live in settlements scattered throughout the West Bank and Gaza, areas captured by Israel in the 1967 Middle East war and home to more than two million Palestinians.
Egypt has intensified its mediation role in the crisis since a summit between Mubarak and Netanyahu last month.

Diplomatic sources said Egypt was pushing a five-point plan which included a freeze on any change in the status of Jerusalem and a ban on Jewish settlement building in the West Bank for "a sufficient period". In return the Palestinians would give a firm commitment to address Israel's security demands.
